blocks.text: Weights and Biases, commonly called W&B, is a widely used experiment tracking and collaboration platform, offering a hosted, richly visual alternative to the open source MLflow covered in the previous topic, with particular strength in real-time monitoring and hyperparameter sweep automation.

This topic covers W&B live dashboard, its automated sweep feature for hyperparameter search, and its collaborative reporting tools that distinguish it from the more infrastructure-focused MLflow approach.

W&B gives a hosted platform for experiment tracking, connecting to the same general experiment tracking concept covered in an earlier topic, with a single logging call from within a training script streaming metrics to a live, richly visual web dashboard as training progresses.

W&B dashboard updates in real time as training runs, showing loss curves, evaluation metrics, and system resource usage, GPU utilization and memory, all updating live, letting a team watch a long-running fine-tuning job progress and catch problems early rather than only reviewing results after training finishes.

code.content:
import wandb

wandb.init(project="fine-tuning-experiments")
wandb.config.learning_rate = 2e-5

for step, loss in enumerate(training_loop()):
    wandb.log({"loss": loss, "step": step})

blocks.text: W&B sweeps feature automates hyperparameter search, defining a range of values to try for parameters like learning rate or LoRA rank, covered in earlier modules, and automatically launching and tracking many runs across that search space, then surfacing which combination performed best.

blocks.text: W&B is built with team collaboration in mind, multiple team members can view and comment on the same experiments, compare each other results, and build on shared past work, a natural fit for teams running many fine-tuning experiments together rather than a single individual working in isolation.
5. Artifacts for Dataset and Model Versioning

blocks.alt: Artifacts for Dataset and Model Versioning

blocks.text: W&B Artifacts feature versions datasets and models, connecting to the dataset versioning and model versioning concepts covered in earlier topics, with a lineage view showing exactly which dataset version and code produced which trained model, a useful traceability feature.

blocks.title: Lineage tracking answers a question that comes up constantly
blocks.content: When a model behaves unexpectedly, being able to trace exactly which dataset version, code version, and hyperparameters produced it is often the fastest path to diagnosing what changed.

blocks.text: The core difference from MLflow, covered in the previous topic, is that W&B is primarily a hosted, managed service with a strong emphasis on visualization and collaboration, MLflow is open source and more commonly self-hosted, teams choose based on whether they prioritize a polished managed experience or open source infrastructure control.

W&B report builder lets a team compile charts, comparisons, and notes into a shareable narrative document, useful for summarizing a series of fine-tuning experiments for stakeholders who were not directly running the experiments themselves.

W&B integrates directly with the Transformers Trainer API and TRL trainer classes, both covered in earlier topics of this module, often requiring just a single configuration flag to start logging a training run, minimizing the setup friction for teams already using these libraries.
9. When Weights and Biases Is a Good Fit

W&B fits teams that value real-time training visibility, automated hyperparameter search, and strong collaborative tooling, particularly teams willing to use a hosted service rather than self-hosting their own experiment tracking infrastructure.

A team running a large hyperparameter search for a fine-tuning project configures a W&B sweep across learning rate and LoRA rank combinations, letting the sweep automatically launch and track dozens of runs rather than manually configuring and monitoring each one individually.

Watching the live dashboard during the sweep, they notice one configuration is diverging early, with the loss curve visibly spiking, and are able to stop that specific run early rather than waiting for it to complete, saving compute, once the sweep finishes, they use the dashboard comparison view to identify the best performing configuration directly.

items: Not monitoring the live dashboard during long training runs, missing an opportunity to catch and stop a diverging run early
Manually configuring hyperparameter search runs one at a time instead of using the sweeps feature to automate it
Choosing W&B without considering that it is primarily a hosted service, a consideration for teams needing full infrastructure control
Not using Artifacts to track dataset and model lineage, losing traceability when diagnosing an unexpected model behavior later

Weights and Biases provides a hosted, richly visual experiment tracking platform with real-time training dashboards, automated hyperparameter sweeps, and strong collaborative tooling, offering a managed alternative to the open source, self-hosted MLflow covered in the previous topic, with particular strength for teams that want live training visibility and easy hyperparameter search automation.
